newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Pakistani plane in emergency landing in Almaty.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani plane in emergency landing in Almaty.

text.p: A Pakistan International Airlines airliner made an emergency landing in Almaty on Monday after smoke was detected in the cabin, an airline spokesman said.

A spokesman of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) in Karachi said flight PK-296 which took off from Almaty for Islamabad-Karachi landed safely back after smoke was detected in the cabin at a height of 2,500 metres (8,200 ft).

He said the 13-member crew and 51 passengers on board the Tupolev-154 were safe in Almaty. He said PIA had made arrangements for a change of aircraft and the flight would soon be airborne for its scheduled destination.

The Tu-154, a three-engined, medium-range passenger plane, is the workhorse of most airlines in the former Soviet Union although some airlines are now switching to Western built Boeing and Airbus jets.
